A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments on four DomainBed datasets, including accuracy, calibration, optimizer comparisons, and three-seed results in Table A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Camelyon17 evaluation and zero-shot CLIP results in Appendix D.3–D.4.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning and validation-based model-selection approach remains unchanged. CLIP is introduced as an existing comparison model, not as a new proposed algorithm or component.

E1.justification: v3 adds Camelyon17 medical-image classification across five hospital domains, extending evaluation beyond the four retained DomainBed datasets to binary histopathology classification. This materially broadens the represented data and distribution shifts (Table 2; Appendix D.3).

E2.justification: v3 adds three zero-shot CLIP reference models using ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and ViT-B/32 encoders (Appendix A.3 and D.4). The original 97 model entries and Table 1's ERM, Best Algorithm, and Best Model comparison remain.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce zero-shot CLIP evaluation with the text template 'a photo of a {class}' and a held-out-hospital evaluation for Camelyon17. Existing fine-tuning settings retain the learning-rate and weight-decay grids, batch size 32, 5,000 iterations, and training-domain validation selection.

E4.justification: The optimizer, weight-decay, random-seed, pre-training-recipe, and ImageNet-shift analyses are retained across the reorganized appendices. The new 'Ablation Study' appendix largely relocates existing analyses; Camelyon17 and CLIP add benchmark and model comparisons rather than new controlled ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and mean plus standard deviation for the same selected models. v2 Table A.2 becomes v3 Table C.1 with unchanged entries. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial accuracy and calibration results for Camelyon17, where reported test accuracies exceed 90%, and zero-shot CLIP results across four DomainBed datasets (Figures D.13–D.14). CLIP exhibits worsening calibration with larger visual encoders. These are additional results under new settings; Table 1 and the three-seed table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ECE, accuracy, and confidence definitions are mathematically unchanged. v3 combines the accuracy and confidence formulas into one numbered display. Neither version supplies new original theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that larger pre-trained models and datasets improve OOD accuracy and calibration, generic pre-training transfers better, and model selection can outperform algorithmic improvements. Expanded experimental coverage supports these retained claims without redefining their central meaning.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about possible CLIP pre-training overlap with evaluation domains and Camelyon17's limited ability to distinguish models because performance is near ceiling. Its conclusion drops v2's explicit real-time deployment limitation and transfer-aware pre-training discussion, while retaining a general call for computationally efficient methods.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds hardware, software versions, licenses, CLIP checkpoint links, and inference instructions. Reported total computation increases from over 100,000 to over 120,000 GPU hours, and the code reference changes from GitHub to an anonymous review repository. Core fine-tuning hyperparameters were already documented in v2.

R1.justification: The introduction and related-work section substantially expand comparisons with previous model-selection studies. v3 adds an Uncertainty Calibration Benchmark discussion, detailed positioning against Minderer and Vishniakov, and CLIP-related literature and scope distinctions. This goes beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the introduction and conclusion, condenses v2's main-text Other Findings section into a summary with details in Appendix B, and reorganizes supplementary material into Appendices A–D with a contents list. The title also changes from 'Investigation' to 'Study'.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v3 merges v2 Figures 3–4, rearranges several plots into horizontal panels, expands Figure 1 with Camelyon17, relocates secondary figures, and adds Figures D.13–D.14 and an appendix dataset table. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens the paper by testing its findings on medical images, exposing different calibration behavior in CLIP, and documenting more reproducibility information. The reorganized appendices also aid navigation. The gains are limited by Camelyon17's near-ceiling performance, CLIP's different evaluation setting and possible domain overlap, and the removal of v2's explicit real-time deployment caveat.
